art.name: Classical Greek & Roman Art
art.significance: Enduring Western ideal of beauty and proportion.
art.summary: Idealized human form in sculpture, architecture (orders), and naturalistic painting.

art.name: Chinese Landscape Painting & Calligraphy
art.significance: Distinct East Asian aesthetic valuing suggestion and emptiness.
art.summary: Ink monochrome landscapes expressing Daoist and literati ideals; calligraphy as high art.

art.name: Renaissance Art
art.significance: Pivot toward modern Western visual culture.
art.summary: Revival of classical forms, linear perspective, humanism, and oil technique.

art.name: Modern & Contemporary Art
art.summary: Impressionism through abstraction, conceptual art, and digital media; challenge to traditional representation.

art.name: Paleolithic Cave Art
art.summary: Paintings and engravings of animals and abstract signs in deep caves (Lascaux, Chauvet, Sulawesi).

biological_and_other_codes.name: Genetic Code
biological_and_other_codes.significance: Central to molecular biology, genetics, and biotechnology.
biological_and_other_codes.summary: Mapping of DNA/RNA nucleotide triplets (codons) to amino acids; nearly universal across life.

biological_and_other_codes.name: Barcode & QR Codes
biological_and_other_codes.significance: Ubiquitous in commerce, tracking, and everyday information exchange.
biological_and_other_codes.summary: Optical machine-readable representations of data for inventory, logistics, and mobile interaction.

biological_and_other_codes.name: Unicode & Character Encoding
biological_and_other_codes.significance: Enables consistent multilingual digital text worldwide.
biological_and_other_codes.summary: Universal character set and encoding standards (UTF-8 dominant) replacing fragmented legacy encodings.

key_concepts: Type Systems (static vs dynamic, strong vs weak)

major_languages_timeline.name: Machine Code & Assembly
major_languages_timeline.notes: Direct binary instructions or mnemonic representations of CPU operations.

major_languages_timeline.name: Fortran
major_languages_timeline.notes: First widely used high-level language; scientific computing.

major_languages_timeline.name: Lisp
major_languages_timeline.notes: List processing; foundational for AI and functional programming.

major_languages_timeline.name: COBOL
major_languages_timeline.notes: Business-oriented; still used in legacy enterprise systems.

major_languages_timeline.name: ALGOL
major_languages_timeline.notes: Influential syntax and block structure; ancestor of many languages.

major_languages_timeline.name: C
major_languages_timeline.notes: Systems programming; portable and close to hardware; foundation of Unix and many later languages.

major_languages_timeline.name: Smalltalk
major_languages_timeline.notes: Pure object-oriented; inspired modern GUI and OOP design.

major_languages_timeline.name: C++
major_languages_timeline.notes: C with classes; multi-paradigm systems and application language.

major_languages_timeline.name: Python
major_languages_timeline.notes: Readable multi-paradigm language; dominant in data science, scripting, education.

major_languages_timeline.name: Java
major_languages_timeline.notes: Write once, run anywhere (JVM); enterprise and Android standard.

major_languages_timeline.name: JavaScript
major_languages_timeline.notes: Originally browser scripting; now full-stack via Node.js and ubiquitous on the web.

major_languages_timeline.name: Rust
major_languages_timeline.notes: Systems language emphasizing memory safety without garbage collection.

major_languages_timeline.name: Go
major_languages_timeline.notes: Simple concurrency model; popular for cloud and networked services.

computer_programming.overview: Formal languages and methods for instructing computers. Evolved from machine code to high-level abstractions.

paradigms.description: Step-by-step instructions that change program state (variables, control flow).
paradigms.name: Imperative / Procedural

paradigms.description: Organization around objects that encapsulate data and behavior; inheritance, polymorphism.
paradigms.name: Object-Oriented

paradigms.description: Computation as evaluation of mathematical functions; immutability, higher-order functions, recursion.
paradigms.name: Functional

paradigms.description: Program as set of logical relations; solver finds solutions.
paradigms.name: Logic / Declarative

paradigms.description: Explicit support for simultaneous execution and communication.
paradigms.name: Concurrent / Parallel

cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.name: Caesar Cipher & Classical Substitution
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.significance: Early systematic cryptography; broken by frequency analysis.
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.summary: Simple shift or monoalphabetic substitution; later polyalphabetic (Vigenère).

cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.name: Morse Code
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.significance: Enabled long-distance electrical communication; still used in emergencies and amateur radio.
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.summary: Variable-length binary encoding of letters and numbers using dots and dashes for telegraph.

cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.name: Enigma & Rotor Machines
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.significance: Breaking Enigma (Polish then Allied efforts) had major wartime impact; spurred modern computing.
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.summary: Electro-mechanical rotor cipher machines used by Germany in WWII.

cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.name: Public-Key Cryptography
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.significance: Foundation of modern secure internet communication (TLS, digital signatures).
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.summary: Asymmetric encryption (RSA, Diffie-Hellman) allowing secure communication without prior shared secret.

cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.name: Error-Correcting Codes
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.significance: Essential for reliable digital communication, storage (CDs, hard drives, deep-space probes).
cryptographic_and_signalling_codes.summary: Mathematical codes that detect and correct transmission or storage errors.

codes.description: Expanded category covering computer programming languages & paradigms, legal codes, cryptographic systems, signalling codes, biological codes, and other structured symbolic systems.

legal_codes.name: Code of Hammurabi
legal_codes.significance: Public monumental law; influence on later Near Eastern legal thought.
legal_codes.summary: One of the earliest extensive written law codes; lex talionis principle, detailed civil and criminal provisions.

legal_codes.name: Twelve Tables
legal_codes.significance: Basis for later Roman legal development and Western legal tradition.
legal_codes.summary: Foundation of Roman law; publicly displayed statutes covering procedure, family, property, and delicts.

legal_codes.name: Justinian Code (Corpus Juris Civilis)
legal_codes.significance: Primary source for civil-law systems in Europe and beyond.
legal_codes.summary: Compilation and rationalization of Roman law under Emperor Justinian.

legal_codes.name: Napoleonic Code (Code Civil)
legal_codes.significance: Model for numerous civil-law jurisdictions worldwide.
legal_codes.summary: Modern civil code emphasizing clarity, equality before the law (for men), and property rights.

legal_codes.name: Common Law Tradition
legal_codes.significance: Foundation of legal systems in UK, USA, Canada, Australia, India (partly), etc.
legal_codes.summary: Judge-made law evolving through precedent (stare decisis) rather than comprehensive codes.

empires.name: Akkadian Empire
empires.significance: Model for later Near Eastern empires; centralized administration and standing army.
empires.summary: First known multi-ethnic empire under Sargon of Akkad.

empires.name: Egyptian New Kingdom
empires.significance: Peak of pharaonic power and cultural influence.
empires.summary: Imperial phase with extensive conquests, monumental building, and international diplomacy.

empires.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
empires.region: Iran → Egypt, Anatolia, Central Asia, Indus
empires.significance: Administrative model later adopted by Alexander and others; Zoroastrian cultural influence.
empires.summary: Largest empire of its time; tolerant administration via satrapies and Royal Road.

empires.name: Roman Empire
empires.region: Mediterranean, Western Europe, North Africa, Near East
empires.significance: Foundational for Western law, language, Christianity, and political concepts.
empires.summary: From republic to principate to dominate; law, engineering, and Latin culture spread widely.

empires.name: Han Dynasty China
empires.significance: Template for later Chinese dynasties; lasting bureaucratic and cultural patterns.
empires.summary: Consolidation of imperial China; Confucian bureaucracy, Silk Road expansion, paper invention.

empires.name: Islamic Caliphates (Rashidun → Abbasid)
empires.region: Arabia → Middle East, North Africa, Iberia, Central Asia
empires.significance: Transmission of classical knowledge; advances in mathematics, medicine, astronomy.
empires.summary: Rapid expansion followed by Golden Age of science, philosophy, and trade.

empires.name: Mongol Empire
empires.significance: Unprecedented connectivity of East and West; demographic and political upheaval.
empires.summary: Unified under Genghis Khan; facilitated Eurasian exchange via Pax Mongolica.

empires.name: British Empire
empires.significance: Spread of English language, common law, industrial technology; decolonization after WWII.
empires.summary: Maritime and colonial expansion driven by trade, industry, and naval power.

literature.name: Ancient Epics & Sacred Texts
literature.significance: Foundational narratives of identity, ethics, and cosmology.

literature.name: Classical & Medieval Literatures
literature.significance: Development of literary forms and vernaculars.

literature.name: Early Modern to 19th Century Novel & Drama
literature.significance: Rise of the novel as dominant form; psychological and social realism.

literature.name: Modern & Contemporary World Literature
literature.significance: Experimentation, diverse voices, and global literary marketplace.

mathematics.name: Babylonian & Egyptian Mathematics
mathematics.summary: Sexagesimal system, algebraic problem tablets, practical geometry for surveying and construction.

mathematics.name: Greek Mathematics
mathematics.summary: Deductive geometry and early number theory; axiomatic method.

mathematics.name: Indian & Islamic Mathematics
mathematics.significance: Transmission and expansion of numerical and algebraic methods to Europe.
mathematics.summary: Decimal place-value system with zero, algebra (al-jabr), trigonometry advances.

mathematics.name: Calculus & Classical Analysis
mathematics.significance: Essential tool for physics, engineering, and later pure mathematics.
mathematics.summary: Independent development of differential and integral calculus; formalization of limits and series.

mathematics.name: Modern Foundations & Abstraction
mathematics.significance: Modern pure mathematics and theoretical computer science foundations.
mathematics.summary: Rigorous analysis, set theory, abstract algebra, topology, and computability.

meta.description: A structured, standalone reference of major historical and conceptual entries. Not exhaustive. Focuses on key milestones, figures, and significance across human history.
meta.notes: Codes section expanded to include computer programming languages & paradigms plus legal, cryptographic, signalling, biological, and other code systems.
meta.title: World Knowledge Base – Technology, Empires, Religions, Mathematics, Art, Codes, Music & Related Domains

music.name: Ancient & Traditional Music Systems
music.summary: Scales, modes, and instruments developed independently; Greek theory of harmonia, Indian raga, Chinese pentatonic, etc.

music.name: Western Classical Tradition
music.significance: Highly developed notated tradition influencing global art music.
music.summary: From Gregorian chant through polyphony, Baroque, Classical, Romantic, to 20th-century modernism.

music.name: Jazz
music.significance: Major 20th-century art form; profound influence on popular music.
music.summary: Improvisational music blending African rhythmic and blues elements with European harmony.

music.name: Popular & Global Contemporary Music
music.significance: Dominant cultural form of the modern era; industry and identity marker.
music.summary: Recording technology enabled mass dissemination; rock, pop, hip-hop, electronic, and countless regional fusions.

philosophy.name: Pre-Socratic & Classical Greek Philosophy
philosophy.summary: Search for arche, ethics, politics, metaphysics, and logic.

philosophy.name: Indian Philosophical Traditions
philosophy.summary: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, Vedanta; Buddhist and Jain schools; debates on self, reality, knowledge.

philosophy.name: Medieval & Early Modern European Philosophy
philosophy.summary: Faith & reason, rationalism vs empiricism, social contract, critical philosophy.

philosophy.name: 19th–20th Century Philosophy
philosophy.summary: Historicism, existentialism, analytic philosophy, phenomenology, political philosophy.

religions.name: Hinduism
religions.significance: One of the oldest continuous religious traditions; profound influence on Indian philosophy and society.
religions.summary: Diverse traditions centered on dharma, karma, samsara, and multiple deities or ultimate reality (Brahman).

religions.name: Buddhism
religions.significance: Major world religion emphasizing ethics, meditation, and non-theistic liberation.
religions.summary: Founded by Siddhartha Gautama; Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path aimed at ending suffering (dukkha).

religions.name: Judaism
religions.significance: Foundation for later Abrahamic religions; enduring cultural and ethical influence.
religions.summary: Monotheistic tradition centered on covenant with Yahweh, Torah, and ethical commandments.

religions.name: Christianity
religions.significance: Largest world religion; shaped Western law, art, calendar, and institutions.
religions.summary: Centered on the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth; Trinitarian theology in most traditions.

religions.name: Islam
religions.significance: Second-largest religion; major civilizational force in science, law, and culture.
religions.summary: Monotheistic faith revealed to Prophet Muhammad; Five Pillars and Quran as central scripture.

religions.name: Confucianism & Daoism
religions.significance: Core of traditional Chinese ethics, governance, and aesthetics.
religions.summary: Confucianism emphasizes social harmony, ritual, and hierarchy; Daoism emphasizes naturalness and the Way (Dao).

science.name: Aristotelian & Medieval Natural Philosophy
science.summary: Qualitative physics, geocentric cosmos, teleology; transmitted and expanded in Islamic and European scholarship.

science.name: Scientific Revolution
science.summary: Heliocentrism, experimental method, mathematical laws of motion and gravity, circulation of blood.

science.name: Chemistry & Periodic Table
science.summary: Modern chemical elements, atomic theory, periodic law.

science.name: Darwinian Evolution & Genetics
science.summary: Natural selection; rediscovery of Mendel; DNA structure and molecular genetics.

science.name: Relativity & Quantum Mechanics
science.summary: Revolution in understanding space, time, gravity, and the microscopic world.

science.name: Big Bang Cosmology & Modern Astrophysics
science.summary: Expanding universe, cosmic microwave background, dark matter/energy, exoplanets.

technology.name: Stone Tools & Control of Fire
technology.significance: Foundation of human technological culture and brain-energy trade-off via cooked food.
technology.summary: Earliest flaked stone tools (Lomekwi, Oldowan, Acheulean) and controlled use of fire enabled cooking, protection, and social gathering.

technology.name: Agricultural Revolution (Neolithic)
technology.region: Fertile Crescent, China, Mesoamerica, Andes, New Guinea
technology.summary: Domestication of plants and animals, permanent settlements, pottery, and early irrigation.

technology.name: Bronze & Iron Ages Metallurgy
technology.significance: Military and agricultural productivity leap; rise of early states.
technology.summary: Smelting of copper alloys then iron; tools, weapons, and trade networks expanded dramatically.

technology.name: Writing Systems
technology.significance: Allowed complex administration, history, and cumulative knowledge.
technology.summary: Cuneiform, hieroglyphs, Chinese characters, and later alphabetic systems enabled record-keeping, law, and literature.

technology.name: Printing Press
technology.region: Europe (Gutenberg); earlier movable type in China/Korea
technology.significance: Catalyst for Renaissance, Reformation, Scientific Revolution, and mass literacy.
technology.summary: Mechanical movable-type printing dramatically lowered cost of books and accelerated knowledge diffusion.

technology.name: Steam Engine & Industrial Revolution
technology.significance: Shift from agrarian to industrial economies; urbanization and modern capitalism.
technology.summary: Newcomen and Watt steam engines powered factories, railways, and ships; mechanized textile and iron production.

technology.name: Electricity & Electronics
technology.significance: Foundation of modern power grids, communication, and computing.
technology.summary: Discovery and application of electromagnetic principles leading to generators, motors, radio, and semiconductors.

technology.name: Digital Computing & Internet
technology.significance: Information age; global instantaneous communication and data processing.
technology.summary: Electronic digital computers, stored-program architecture, personal computers, and packet-switched networks.

technology.name: Biotechnology & CRISPR
technology.significance: Ability to read and rewrite genetic information; medicine, agriculture, ethics debates.
technology.summary: Recombinant DNA, sequencing, and precise gene-editing tools.
